text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Canadian opposition leader Preston Manning seeks rights for unborn: Reform Party leader sees referendum as route to constitutional amendment.
- Former Quebec Premier Jacques Parizeau unsettles Bouchard with attack on successor's ties to federalists, attempt to eliminate deficit.
- 'Most effective assassin' gets life in jail: Gasps, laughter greet sentencing of former South African police colonel.
-Endangered species left to provinces' care: Federal government wants to shield birds and beasts living on federal land.
- Smokers to get late-night reprieve: Toronto suburb phasing in smoking ban.
- Gulf Canada Resources Ltd. moving key people to U.S.: Oil firm aims to enhance international profile by relocating CEO, executives to Denver.
- Ontario, Bombardier at odds on de Havilland: Province wants new deal on sale of Toronto aircraft maker.
- Nesbitt Burns Inc. faces another derivatives lawsuit: Thunder Bay credit union cites losses.
- A family buries the cleaver: The Mitchells have made peace after a nasty two-year family fight for control of their meat-packing business.

- Gulf Canada Resources Ltd. moves its elite to U.S.: CEO J.P. Bryan will lead 20 to 25 top executives to offices in Denver, but he says the company will remain Canadian with its headquarters in Calgary.
- The man who sold Bre-X's US$38 billion motherlode for just US$6 million.
- VSE delists Cam-Net Communications Network Inc. after FBI sting.
